id: ml-05
title: Multi-similarity loss
paper: Wang et al., Multi-Similarity Loss with General Pair Weighting for Deep Metric Learning (CVPR 2019; arXiv Apr 2019)
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06627
type: Benchmark
cutoff: 2019-04-14
domain: ml
profile: method-benchmark

## expected_verdict
Conditional limitation. The General Pair Weighting framework and the MS loss are valid contributions. The "large margin over state of the art" mostly disappears under a level playing field: same backbone, embedding size, hyperparameter search, and no test-set feedback. There, MS and MS+Miner land within about a point of the classic contrastive loss.

## I0
Does multi-similarity training improve metric-learning retrieval?

## evidence
- Method: General Pair Weighting (GPW) view of pair losses; MS loss combining self-similarity and relative similarities, with iterative pair mining and soft weighting (Eq. 14).
- Data: CUB-200 (first 100 classes train / 100 test), Cars-196, Stanford Online Products (11,318 train / 11,316 test classes), In-Shop Clothes.
- Setup: BN-Inception pretrained on ImageNet; embedding size up to 512.
- Claims: SOTA on all four; e.g. +5.0% Recall@1 over ABE on CUB-200, +7.1% over HTL on In-Shop; In-Shop Recall@1 raised from 80.9% (HTL) to 88.0%.
- Comparisons drawn from prior papers with different backbones and settings; code released.

## intake
- Scope: MS loss improves image-retrieval Recall@K over prior pair-based losses.
- Regime: four standard retrieval benchmarks, BN-Inception, fixed train/test class splits.
- Assumptions: competitor numbers are comparable (same backbone, embedding size, augmentation); hyperparameters were not tuned on the test set.
- Falsifier: under identical pipelines and validation-based tuning, MS is not better than older losses (contrastive, triplet).

## screen
- Must flag: cross-paper numbers mix backbones and embedding sizes; no validation split (test-set feedback); Recall@1 is a weak metric.
- Must request: an equal-pipeline comparison with validation-based hyperparameter search and MAP@R.

## retrieval
- Pre-cutoff must-finds: contrastive (Hadsell et al. 2006) and triplet losses; lifted structure (Song et al.); N-pairs (Sohn); ABE and HTL (direct comparators); binomial deviance.
- Current mode: Musgrave et al. 2020: flaws are unfair comparisons, training with test-set feedback, weak metrics; under fixed BN-Inception, embedding size and Bayesian hyperparameter search with cross-validation, MS / MS+Miner score close to the contrastive loss on CUB-200 (Table 4; check row alignment in the PDF).

## designer
- Hold the pipeline fixed (backbone, embedding 128/512, batch size, augmentation, optimizer); vary only the loss; tune each loss with the same search budget on a validation split; report P@1, R-Precision, MAP@R over ≥ 3 seeds.

## champion
- Contrastive and triplet losses with tuned margins in the identical pipeline (Musgrave's powerful-benchmarker).

## panel
- Flaws: confounded comparisons and no validation split. Repair: rerun under the fixed protocol; keep GPW as a conceptual contribution.

## run
- pytorch-metric-learning on CUB-200 with fixed BN-Inception: train contrastive and MS with equal search; expect overlapping MAP@R.

## verdict
- Label: Conditional limitation: claimed margin explained by protocol differences; loss is competitive, not superior.
- Must say: gains largely vanish under fair comparison; the framework remains valid.
- Must not say: MS loss is broken; or MS is clearly SOTA.

## audit
- Check: +5.0% / +7.1% claims; In-Shop 80.9 → 88.0; Musgrave's three flaws; confirm MS and MS+Miner rows in Musgrave Tables 4–6.

## variants
- Regimes where the loss matters more than the backbone (fine-grained, small data, harder negatives), still under the fixed protocol.
